222.name: Beginner
222.summary: Layer by layer, the 3×3 corner steps on a smaller puzzle.

steps.title: First layer
steps.text: Solve four corners of one colour so their side colours match.

algs.name: Corner insertion
algs.alg: R U R' U'
algs.note: Hold the corner above its slot, at front right, or in its slot when it is twisted there. Repeat until it is solved, five times at most.

picture.from: R U' F2 U R' F U2 R' U' F' R U2
picture.done: R U R' U' R' F R2 U' R' U' R U R' F' R U2 R' U' R U' R'

tips: Choose one corner as the reference; the others are placed around it.

steps.title: Orient the last layer
steps.text: Turn the top face one colour, for example by repeating the Sune (R U R' U R U2 R').

algs.name: Sune
algs.alg: R U R' U R U2 R'
algs.note: One yellow corner on top: hold it at front left. None: hold the front-left corner with yellow on its left side. Two: hold it with yellow facing front. Repeat until the face is done.

picture.done: R U R' U' R' F R2 U' R' U' R U R' F'

steps.title: Permute the last layer
steps.text: Swap the top corners into place with one algorithm, repeated once if needed.

algs.name: Adjacent swap
algs.alg: R U R' U' R' F R2 U' R' U' R U R' F'
algs.note: Two corners with matching sides (headlights): hold them on the left.

algs.name: Diagonal swap
algs.alg: F R U' R' U' R U R' F' R U R' U' R' F R F'
algs.note: No headlights on any side.

222.name: Ortega
222.summary: A fast method with only a dozen algorithms: face, orientation, then both layers at once.

steps.title: First face
steps.text: Make one face a single colour. The side colours do not need to match yet.
tips: Plan the whole face during inspection: it takes four or five moves.
Pick the colour whose face is quickest, usually white or yellow.

help.name: White on top
help.alg: R U2 R' U' R U R'
help.note: Turned to face the side first, then inserted as one of the two others.

picture.from: R U' F2 U R' F U2 R' U' F' R U2
picture.done: R2 U' B2 U2 R2 U' R2 U' D2 R U2 R' U' R U' R'

steps.title: OLL
steps.text: Turn the opposite face one colour with one of 7 algorithms.

picture.done: R2 U' B2 U2 R2 U' R2 U' D2

steps.title: PBL
steps.text: Permute both layers at once with one of 5 algorithms.

222.name: CLL
222.summary: One more look saved: after a full first layer, one algorithm solves the rest.

steps.title: First layer
steps.text: Solve a complete first layer, with matching side colours.
tips: Plan the whole layer during inspection.
Build it on the bottom, so the top is in view for recognition.

help.name: White on top
help.alg: R U2 R' U' R U R'
help.note: Turned to face the side first, then inserted as one of the two others.

picture.from: R U' F2 U R' F U2 R' U' F' R U2
picture.done: R U R' U' R' F R2 U' R' U' R U R' F' R U2 R' U' R U' R'

steps.title: CLL
steps.text: Orient and permute the last layer in one algorithm (42 cases).

222.name: EG
222.summary: The top-level method: a single face, then one algorithm for the whole cube.

steps.title: First face
steps.text: Make one face a single colour; the first layer may be solved, adjacent-swapped or diagonal-swapped.
tips: Recognise the bottom layer during inspection: solved, adjacent swap or diagonal swap.

help.name: White on top
help.alg: R U2 R' U' R U R'
help.note: Turned to face the side first, then inserted as one of the two others.

picture.from: R U' F2 U R' F U2 R' U' F' R U2
picture.done: R2 U' B2 U2 R2 U' R2 U' D2 R U2 R' U' R U' R'

steps.title: CLL, EG-1 or EG-2
steps.text: Recognise the case and solve both layers in one algorithm: CLL, EG-1 or EG-2 depending on the first layer, 42 cases each.

333.name: Beginner
333.summary: Layer by layer with a handful of short algorithms. Slow but reliable, and the base of every other method.

steps.title: White cross
steps.text: Place the four white edges around the white centre so their side colours match the side centres.

picture.from: D2 F2 U' B2 R2 U2 F2 L2 U' R2 U' F' D' R' B L' R D2 U' F' R' z2
picture.done: R U R' U' R' F R2 U' R' U' R U R' F' R U2 R' U' R U' R' F U R U' R' F' U F U R U' R' F' U' F' U F U R U' R' U2 L' U L U F U' F' R U R' U' L' U L B U2 B' z2

tips: Start with a daisy: the four white edges around the yellow centre, white facing up.
Turn the top until an edge's side colour matches the centre below it, then turn that face twice to bring it down.
Hold the cube white side down from here on.

help.name: Edge at the bottom, white down
help.note: Turn the top until no petal is above it, then turn that face twice.
help.setup: F2 R2 B2 L2 U F2 U

help.name: Edge at the bottom, white facing you
help.note: F' brings it into the middle layer, U' frees the slot above it, R brings it up.
help.setup: F2 R2 B2 L2 U R' U F

help.name: Edge in the middle layer
help.note: White on the right, no petal on top in front: one turn of the front brings it up.
help.setup: F2 R2 B2 L2 U F

help.name: Edge on top, white facing you
help.note: F sends it to the right, U' frees the slot above it, R brings it back up white on top.
help.setup: F2 R2 B2 L2 U R' U F'

help.name: Petal to the cross
help.note: Turn the top until its side colour is over its centre, then turn that face twice.

steps.title: First-layer corners
steps.text: Bring each white corner under its slot and repeat R U R' U' until it drops in correctly.

algs.name: Corner insertion
algs.alg: R U R' U'
algs.note: Hold the corner above its slot, at front right, or in its slot when it is twisted there. Repeat until it is solved, five times at most.

picture.from: R U R' U' R' F R2 U' R' U' R U R' F' R U2 R' U' R U' R' F U R U' R' F' U F U R U' R' F' U' F' U F U R U' R' U2 L' U L U F U' F' R U R' U' L' U L B U2 B'
picture.done: R U R' U' R' F R2 U' R' U' R U R' F' R U2 R' U' R U' R' F U R U' R' F' U F U R U' R' F' U' F' U F U R U' R' U2 L' U L U F U' F'

tips: Turn the top until the corner sits above the slot between its two side colours.

steps.title: Second-layer edges
steps.text: Insert the four middle edges from the top layer with the left or right insertion algorithm.

picture.done: R U R' U' R' F R2 U' R' U' R U R' F' R U2 R' U' R U' R' F U R U' R' F' U F U R U' R' F'

algs.name: Right insertion
algs.alg: U R U' R' U' F' U F
algs.note: The edge's front colour matches the front centre and its top colour is the right centre.

algs.name: Left insertion
algs.alg: U' L' U L U F U' F'
algs.note: The edge's front colour matches the front centre and its top colour is the left centre.

tips: Look for a top edge without yellow.
An edge stuck in the wrong slot comes out when any top edge is inserted there.

steps.title: Yellow cross
steps.text: Look at the yellow edges on top, ignoring the corners: none (a dot), two side by side (an L) or two across (a line). Hold the cube as the case says, then flip them with its algorithm.

picture.done: R U R' U' R' F R2 U' R' U' R U R' F' R U2 R' U' R U' R'

algs.name: Dot
algs.alg: F R U R' U' F'
algs.setup: f U R U' R' f' F U R U' R' F'
algs.note: No yellow edge on top: do the line's algorithm from any side, you get an L. Turn the top until the L is at the back left, then do the L.

algs.name: L
algs.alg: F U R U' R' F'
algs.note: Turn the top until the L sits at the back left (yellow edges at the back and on the left), then do it once. The line's algorithm done twice works too: the first makes the line.

algs.name: Line
algs.alg: F R U R' U' F'
algs.note: Hold the line horizontal, from left to right, then do it once: the cross is made.

tips: Only the four edges count here: the corners are done in the next step.
Keep the white face on the bottom: only the top layer changes.

steps.title: Yellow face
steps.text: Turn the yellow corners up with the Sune alone, R U R' U R U2 R'. Count the yellow corners already up, hold the cube as that count says, do the Sune, then look again: three Sunes at most.

picture.done: R U R' U' R' F R2 U' R' U' R U R' F'

algs.name: Sune
algs.alg: (R U R' U R U2 R')
algs.setup: R U2 R' U' R U' R'
algs.note: One yellow corner up: hold it at the front left. One Sune solves it.

algs.name: Antisune
algs.alg: (R U R' U R U2 R') U2 (R U R' U R U2 R')
algs.setup: R U R' U R U2 R' U2
algs.note: One yellow corner up: hold it at the front left. The Sune makes the Sune case: hold its yellow corner at the front left again.

algs.name: H
algs.alg: (R U R' U R U2 R')2
algs.setup: R U2 R' U' R U R' U' R U' R'
algs.note: No yellow corner up: turn the top until the front-left corner shows its yellow on the left. After one Sune a single corner is up, already at the front left.

algs.name: Pi
algs.alg: (R U R' U R U2 R') U' (R U R' U R U2 R')
algs.setup: R' U2 R2 U R2 U R2 U2 R'
algs.note: No yellow corner up: turn the top until the front-left corner shows its yellow on the left. One Sune leaves one corner up: put it at the front left.

algs.name: Headlights
algs.alg: (R U R' U R U2 R') U' (R U R' U R U2 R') U2 (R U R' U R U2 R')
algs.setup: R U2 R D R' U2 R D' R2
algs.note: Two yellow corners up: turn the top until the front-left corner shows its yellow to the front. Each Sune leaves a new case: count again and hold it as it says.

algs.name: T
algs.alg: (R U R' U R U2 R') U (R U R' U R U2 R') U2 (R U R' U R U2 R')
algs.setup: F R' F' r U R U' r'
algs.note: Two yellow corners up: turn the top until the front-left corner shows its yellow to the front. Each Sune leaves a new case: count again and hold it as it says.

algs.name: Bowtie
algs.alg: (R U R' U R U2 R')2 U2 (R U R' U R U2 R')
algs.setup: r U R' U' r' F R F'
algs.note: Two yellow corners up: turn the top until the front-left corner shows its yellow to the front. Each Sune leaves a new case: count again and hold it as it says.

tips: No yellow corner up: turn the top until the front-left corner shows its yellow on the left.
One yellow corner up (the fish): turn the top until it sits at the front left.
Two yellow corners up: turn the top until the front-left corner shows its yellow to the front.

steps.title: Last layer permutation
steps.text: Swap the corners into place, then cycle the edges to finish the cube.

algs.name: Corner cycle
algs.alg: R' F R' B2 R F' R' B2 R2
algs.note: Hold two corners with matching sides (headlights) at the back. None: do it once from any side and look again.

algs.name: Edge cycle · Ua
algs.alg: R U' R U R U R U' R' U' R2
algs.note: Hold the solved edge at the back; the front edge belongs on the right. No solved edge: do it once and look again.

algs.name: Edge cycle · Ub
algs.alg: R2 U R U R' U' R' U' R' U R'
algs.note: Hold the solved edge at the back; the front edge belongs on the left.

333.name: CFOP
333.summary: The most popular speed method: Cross, F2L, OLL and PLL. Most Qbix sets for the 3×3 follow it.

steps.title: Cross
steps.text: Solve the four bottom edges in about eight moves. Plan the whole cross during inspection.

picture.from: D2 F2 U' B2 R2 U2 F2 L2 U' R2 U' F' D' R' B L' R D2 U' F' R'
picture.done: R U R' U' R' F R2 U' R' U' R U R' F' R U2 R' U' R U' R' F U R U' R' F' U F U R U' R' F' U' F' U F U R U' R' U2 L' U L U F U' F' R U R' U' L' U L B U2 B'

tips: Build it on the bottom from the start, so the pairs stay in view.
Place edges relative to each other first; the centres can be matched with one last turn.
Most crosses take eight moves or fewer: if yours takes more, look for a shorter one.

help.name: Edge on top, white up
help.note: Turn the top until its side colour is over its centre, then turn that face twice.

help.name: Edge on top, white facing you
help.note: The edge in front, its other colour above the front centre: R' and R put the right edge back.

help.name: Edge in the middle layer
help.note: White on the right, its other colour on the front: one turn of the front brings it down.

help.name: Edge in its place, flipped
help.note: White facing out at the bottom: D and D' put the other cross edges back.

help.name: Two edges swapped side by side
help.note: The front and right edges each in the other's place.

help.name: Two edges swapped across
help.note: The front and back edges each in the other's place.

steps.title: F2L
steps.text: Pair a corner with its edge and insert them together into their slot, four times. The 41 basic cases are learnt intuitively first.

picture.done: R U R' U' R' F R2 U' R' U' R U R' F' R U2 R' U' R U' R' F U R U' R' F' U F U R U' R' F'

steps.title: OLL
steps.text: Make the top face one colour in a single algorithm (57 cases), or in two steps with 2-look OLL (10 algorithms).

picture.done: R U R' U' R' F R2 U' R' U' R U R' F'

steps.title: PLL
steps.text: Move the last-layer pieces into place in a single algorithm (21 cases), or with 2-look PLL (6 algorithms).

steps.title: Going further
steps.text: WV and VLS orient the last layer while inserting the last pair; COLL and OLLCP leave only an edge PLL. When the last-layer edges are already oriented after F2L, ZBLL solves the whole last layer in one algorithm.

picture.from: R U R' U' R' F R2 U' R' U' R U R' F' R U2 R' U' R U' R' R U R'

333.name: Roux
333.summary: A block-building method with a low move count, finished with M-slice and U turns.

steps.title: First block
steps.text: Build a 1×2×3 block on the left, at the bottom.
tips: Plan the edge and one of the pairs during inspection.
Build the 1×2×2 square first, then add the back pair.

help.name: Front pair, split
help.note: The corner above its slot, its edge on top: L' U' L joins them and drops them into the front of the block.

help.name: Back pair, split
help.note: The same, for the back of the block.

picture.from: D2 F2 U' B2 R2 U2 F2 L2 U' R2 U' F' D' R' B L' R D2 U' F' R'
picture.done: M' U2 M U M' U2 M U' R U2 R' U' R U' R' U R U' R' U2 R U R2 U' R2

steps.title: Second block
steps.text: Build the matching 1×2×3 block on the right using R, r, U and M turns, keeping the first block intact.
tips: Place the bottom edge first, then insert the two pairs as in F2L.
Free M turns help: the middle slice is not solved yet.

help.name: Front pair, split
help.note: The corner above its slot, white facing right, its edge at the back: R U R' joins them and drops them in.

help.name: Front pair, joined
help.note: The pair already made on top: R U' R' drops it into the front slot.

help.name: Back pair, split
help.note: The same as the front pair, for the back slot.

picture.done: M' U2 M U M' U2 M U' R U2 R' U' R U' R' U

steps.title: CMLL
steps.text: Orient and permute the four top corners in one algorithm (42 cases).

picture.done: M' U2 M U M' U2 M U'

algs.name: Sune
algs.alg: R U R' U R U2 R'

algs.name: Antisune
algs.alg: R U2 R' U' R U' R'

algs.name: H
algs.alg: R U R' U R U' R' U R U2 R'

algs.name: Pi
algs.alg: R U2 R2 U' R2 U' R2 U2 R

algs.name: U
algs.alg: R2 D R' U2 R D' R' U2 R'

algs.name: T
algs.alg: r U R' U' r' F R F'

algs.name: L
algs.alg: F R' F' r U R U' r'

algs.name: Adjacent swap
algs.alg: R U R' U' R' F R2 U' R' U' R U R' F'
algs.note: Corners oriented: the two corners with matching sides go on the left.

algs.name: Diagonal swap
algs.alg: F R U' R' U' R U R' F' R U R' U' R' F R F'
algs.note: Corners oriented, no two with matching sides.

tips: The nine algorithms below are two-look CMLL, to start with: orient the corners, then swap them. The top edges may move freely.

steps.title: LSE
steps.text: Solve the last six edges with only M and U turns: orient them, place the left and right edges, then finish the middle slice.

algs.name: Middle cycle
algs.alg: M' U2 M U2
algs.note: Cycles the edges of the middle slice: the front top edge goes down to the front bottom.

algs.name: Middle cycle, reverse
algs.alg: M U2 M' U2
algs.note: The front top edge goes to the back top.

algs.name: Double swap
algs.alg: M2 U2 M2 U2
algs.note: Swaps the two top middle edges and the two bottom ones.

tips: An edge is oriented when its white or yellow sticker faces up or down.
Orient all six first, then place the left and right edges, then the middle slice.

333.name: ZZ
333.summary: Orient every edge first, so the rest of the solve needs no cube rotations and no F or B turns.

steps.title: EOLine
steps.text: Orient all twelve edges and place the front and back bottom edges. EOCross places all four bottom edges instead.
tips: An edge is bad when an R, L, U or D move alone cannot fix it: count the bad edges during inspection.
F or B turns flip four edges at once: use them to bring the count to zero.

help.name: Four bad edges on the front
help.note: One turn of the front flips its four edges.

help.name: Four bad edges at the back
help.note: One turn of the back flips its four edges.

picture.from: D2 F2 U' B2 R2 U2 F2 L2 U' R2 U' F' D' R' B L' R D2 U' F' R'
picture.done: R U R' U' R' F R2 U' R' U' R U R' F' R U2 R' U' R U' R' R U R' U' R U2 R' L' U L R U' R' U2 L' U' L

steps.title: F2L
steps.text: Build the left and right blocks using only R, U and L turns.
tips: No rotations: build the left block with L and U, the right one with R and U.
Every edge stays oriented, so pairs never need F or B turns.

help.name: Front pair, split
help.note: The corner above its slot, white facing right, its edge at the back: R U R' joins them and drops them in.

help.name: Front pair, joined
help.note: The pair already made on top: R U' R' drops it into the front slot.

help.name: Back pair, split
help.note: The same as the front pair, for the back slot.

picture.done: R U R' U' R' F R2 U' R' U' R U R' F' R U2 R' U' R U' R'

steps.title: Last layer
steps.text: Edges are already oriented, so ZBLL finishes in one algorithm; otherwise orient the corners, then use PLL.
tips: Only the corner cases of 2-Look OLL appear: the edges are already oriented.

444.name: Reduction
444.summary: Turn the 4×4 into a big 3×3: build the centres, pair the edges, then solve it like a 3×3.

steps.title: Centres
steps.text: Each face has 4 centre pieces and no fixed centre, so place the colours in the standard scheme yourself: white opposite yellow, green opposite blue, then check the order around. Build the first two opposite centres, then the last four, taking care not to break the finished ones.
tips: Build each centre as bars first, then join the bars.
Use only slice moves and the face you are building on, so finished centres stay intact.

picture.from: R Uw2 F' 2R Bw2 U L' Fw D2 Rw' 2F B2 Uw' R2 2U F Lw2 D' 2B Rw U' 2L F2 Dw 3R 3Uw' 3F2 3Dw B 3L'
picture.done: D2 F2 U' B2 R2 U2 F2 L2 U' R2 U' F' D' R' B L' R D2 U' F' R' 2U R U R' F R' F' R 2U' 2D' L' U' L F' L F L' 2D

steps.title: Edge pairing
steps.text: Join the 2 edge pieces of each edge into one bar. Match pieces on the inner slices, pair them with a flip, then restore the centres with the reverse slice move.
tips: Pair edges on the front and back of the middle row, never on the top or bottom.
Always undo the slice move after the flip, or the centres break.

picture.done: D2 F2 U' B2 R2 U2 F2 L2 U' R2 U' F' D' R' B L' R D2 U' F' R'

steps.title: 3×3 stage
steps.text: Only the outer layers move from here: solve the cube with your 3×3 method (cross, F2L, OLL, PLL).
tips: The big cube turns more slowly: look ahead rather than turning faster.

steps.title: Parity
steps.text: Two parities are special to even cubes: OLL parity (a single flipped edge) and PLL parity (two swapped edges). Each is fixed with one long algorithm when it appears.

picture.from: F2 2R2 F2 U2 2R U2 2R' U2 2R2 F2 2L F2 2L' U2 2R

444.name: Yau
444.summary: The method used by most fast solvers: the cross is built during the centres, so the edges can be paired with more freedom.

steps.title: First two centres
steps.text: Solve two opposite centres, usually white and yellow, and hold white on the left.

picture.from: R Uw2 F' 2R Bw2 U L' Fw D2 Rw' 2F B2 Uw' R2 2U F Lw2 D' 2B Rw U' 2L F2 Dw 3R 3Uw' 3F2 3Dw B 3L'
picture.done: R U R' U' R' F R2 U' R' U' R U R' F' R U2 R' U' R U' R' F U R U' R' F' U F U R U' R' F' U' F' U F U R U' R' U2 L' U L U F U' F' R U R' U' L' U L B U2 B' B2 2U R U R' F R' F' R 2U' 2U2 2D' R2 L2

steps.title: Three cross edges
steps.text: Pair three white edges and place them around the white centre.
tips: Plan the first edge during inspection.
Pair each edge with one slice move and insert it on the left without breaking the centres.

picture.done: R U R' U' R' F R2 U' R' U' R U R' F' R U2 R' U' R U' R' F U R U' R' F' U F U R U' R' F' U' F' U F U R U' R' U2 L' U L U F U' F' R U R' U' L' U L B U2 B' B2 2U R U R' F R' F' R 2U' 2U2 2D'

steps.title: Last four centres
steps.text: Build the remaining centres without disturbing the three cross edges.
tips: Keep the cross edges on the left face: only the right and the inner slices move freely.

picture.done: R U R' U' R' F R2 U' R' U' R U R' F' R U2 R' U' R U' R' F U R U' R' F' U F U R U' R' F' U' F' U F U R U' R' U2 L' U L U F U' F' R U R' U' L' U L B U2 B' B2 2U R U R' F R' F' R 2U'

steps.title: Last cross edge and pairing
steps.text: Pair and place the last cross edge, turn white to the bottom, then pair the eight remaining edges, usually three, then two, then three at a time.

picture.done: R U R' U' R' F R2 U' R' U' R U R' F' R U2 R' U' R U' R' F U R U' R' F' U F U R U' R' F' U' F' U F U R U' R' U2 L' U L U F U' F' R U R' U' L' U L B U2 B'

steps.title: 3×3 stage
steps.text: The cross is already done: finish with F2L, OLL and PLL. Two parities are special to even cubes: OLL parity (a single flipped edge) and PLL parity (two swapped edges). Each is fixed with one long algorithm when it appears.

555.name: Reduction
555.summary: Turn the 5×5 into a big 3×3: build the centres, pair the edges, then solve it like a 3×3.

steps.title: Centres
steps.text: Each face has 9 centre pieces; the middle one is fixed and sets the colour of the face. Build the first two opposite centres, then the last four, taking care not to break the finished ones.
tips: Build each centre as bars first, then join the bars.
Use only slice moves and the face you are building on, so finished centres stay intact.

picture.from: R Uw2 F' 2R Bw2 U L' Fw D2 Rw' 2F B2 Uw' R2 2U F Lw2 D' 2B Rw U' 2L F2 Dw 3R 3Uw' 3F2 3Dw B 3L'
picture.done: D2 F2 U' B2 R2 U2 F2 L2 U' R2 U' F' D' R' B L' R D2 U' F' R' 2U R U R' F R' F' R 2U' 2D' L' U' L F' L F L' 2D

steps.title: Edge pairing
steps.text: Join the 3 edge pieces of each edge into one bar. Match pieces on the inner slices, pair them with a flip, then restore the centres with the reverse slice move.
tips: Pair edges on the front and back of the middle row, never on the top or bottom.
Always undo the slice move after the flip, or the centres break.

picture.done: D2 F2 U' B2 R2 U2 F2 L2 U' R2 U' F' D' R' B L' R D2 U' F' R'

steps.title: 3×3 stage

steps.title: 3×3 stage
steps.text: The cross is already done: finish with F2L, OLL and PLL. Odd cubes have no OLL or PLL parity: the only parity appears while pairing the last two edges and is fixed with one algorithm.

sq1.name: Beginner
sq1.summary: Restore the cube shape, then fix the pieces one property at a time with short algorithms.

steps.title: Cube shape
steps.text: Return both layers to a square with the known shape sequences, keeping the middle layer aligned.

steps.title: Orient corners
steps.text: Bring every top-colour corner to the top and every bottom-colour corner to the bottom.

steps.title: Orient edges
steps.text: Do the same with the edges.

steps.title: Permute corners
steps.text: Swap corners until both layers have their corners in place.

steps.title: Permute edges
steps.text: Cycle the edges into place.

steps.title: Parity
steps.text: If two pieces stay swapped or the middle layer is flipped, apply the parity algorithm.

sq1.name: Vandenbergh
sq1.summary: The standard speed method: the same steps, merged into fewer looks with more algorithms.

steps.title: Cube shape
steps.text: Solve the shape efficiently during inspection; advanced solvers also track parity here.

steps.title: CO/EO
steps.text: Orient corners, then edges, each in one algorithm.

steps.title: CP
steps.text: Permute the corners of both layers in one algorithm.
steps.missing: Qbix holds the beginner corner cases; the full one-look CP set is not in it yet.

steps.title: EP
steps.text: Permute the edges of both layers, recognising parity cases in the same step.
steps.missing: The full EP set is not in Qbix yet.

pyram.name: Layer by layer
pyram.summary: Tips first, then the bottom layer and the last three edges.

steps.title: Tips
steps.text: Turn each of the four small tips to match the centre below it. They move independently of everything else.
tips: The lowercase moves u, r, l and b turn one tip each.

steps.title: Centres
steps.text: Align the three centres around one corner with a colour on the bottom face.
tips: Each centre turns with the corner above it: one move per centre at most.

steps.title: Bottom edges
steps.text: Insert the three bottom edges one by one with short insertions.

steps.title: Last three edges
steps.text: Solve the top edges with one of a few algorithms, such as the Sledge (R' L R L').

pyram.name: L4E
pyram.summary: A faster method: a small V block, then the last four edges in one algorithm.

steps.title: Tips
steps.text: Solve the tips, or leave them for the end since they only need one turn each.
tips: Leaving the tips for the end saves looking at them twice.

steps.title: V
steps.text: Solve three centres and two edges around one corner, forming a V shape.
tips: Plan the whole V during inspection: it takes four or five moves.

steps.title: Last four edges
steps.text: Place the last four edges with one algorithm chosen from their position and orientation.
steps.missing: The L4E algorithms are not in Qbix yet.

skewb.name: Beginner
skewb.summary: A first layer, then the top corners and the centres with two repeated sequences.

steps.title: First layer
steps.text: Solve one centre and its four corners so their side colours agree.
tips: Start from the centre, then add the corners one at a time with short insertions.
Check that each corner agrees with its two neighbours on the sides.

steps.title: Top corners
steps.text: Orient and place the top corners by repeating the Sledgehammer (R' L R L') or the Sune.

steps.title: Centres
steps.text: Cycle the last centres into place with the centre algorithm.

skewb.name: Sarah's intermediate
skewb.summary: A popular speed method with a small set of algorithms.

steps.title: First layer
steps.text: Solve one face and its four corners, usually planned during inspection.
tips: Plan the whole layer during inspection: it takes four or five moves.

steps.title: Top corners
steps.text: Solve the four remaining corners in one algorithm chosen by their orientation.
steps.missing: Qbix holds the basic corner cases; the full intermediate set is not in it yet.

steps.title: Last five centres
steps.text: Place the remaining centres with a single algorithm (L5C).
steps.missing: Qbix holds the two centre cycles; the other L5C cases are not in it yet.

minx.name: Layer by layer
minx.summary: The 3×3 beginner approach, spread over twelve faces.

steps.title: Star
steps.text: Place the five edges around the first centre.
tips: Like the 3×3 cross: match each edge with its side centre.

steps.title: First layer
steps.text: Insert the five corners around it, as on the 3×3.

algs.name: Corner insertion
algs.alg: R U R' U'
algs.note: Hold the corner above its slot, at front right, and repeat until it is solved.

steps.title: Middle layers
steps.text: Insert the edges, then the corner and edge pairs, face by face, until only the last face remains.

steps.title: Last layer
steps.text: Orient the last-layer edges, then the corners, then permute corners and edges.

minx.name: S2L and 4-look
minx.summary: The standard speed approach: pairs and blocks, then the last layer in four algorithms.

steps.title: Star and F2L
steps.text: Build the star, then insert five corner and edge pairs as in 3×3 F2L.

steps.title: S2L
steps.text: Build the next layers with blocks on the side faces until only the last face remains.
tips: Solve one side face at a time, as a block of two pairs and its edges.
Keep the unsolved faces at the top, so the blocks stay in view.

steps.title: Last layer
steps.text: Orient the edges, orient the corners, permute the edges, then permute the corners.

clock.name: Beginner
clock.summary: Solve the front cross, then the back cross, then the corners.

steps.title: Front cross
steps.text: Use pin settings to bring the four edge dials to the same time as the centre, then turn the whole cross to 12.
steps.missing: The Clock's pin settings are not in Qbix yet.

steps.title: Back cross
steps.text: Flip the clock and solve the other cross, with pin settings that leave the first one untouched.
steps.missing: The Clock's pin settings are not in Qbix yet.

steps.title: Corners
steps.text: Turn each corner to 12, one pin up at a time. Each corner dial is linked to the one behind it, so both sides finish together.
tips: With one pin up, the wheel next to it turns that corner alone.
Flip the clock when a corner of the front is still off: its back corner moves with it.

clock.name: 7-simul
clock.summary: The speed method: seven steps with the same pin settings every solve, turning two wheels at once.

steps.title: Read
steps.text: During inspection, read the dials and work out how far each of the seven steps must turn.
tips: Read the front dials first, then the back ones.
Learn the seven pin settings by heart: only the amounts change.

steps.title: Solve
steps.text: Apply the steps of the first side, flip the clock and apply the rest. Only the amounts change from one scramble to the next.
steps.missing: The 7-simul sequences are not in Qbix yet.

333.name: Old Pochmann
333.summary: The first blindfolded method: one piece at a time, each swapped into place with the T perm (edges) or the Y perm (corners), a setup before and undone after.

steps.title: Memo
steps.text: Every sticker has a letter (Speffz: A to X, face by face). From the buffer, UR for the edges and UBL for the corners, note the letter where its piece belongs, then where the piece there belongs, until the buffer's piece comes back. Group the letters in pairs and turn each pair into a word or an image.
tips: Edges first, then corners: the memo is read in the order the cube is solved.
When the buffer's piece comes home with pieces still wrong, start a new cycle on one of them and end on it again.
Train the memo of a scramble and your letter pairs in Training → BLD.

steps.title: Edges
steps.text: Hold white on top, green in front. For each edge letter, bring the target to UL with L and D turns and their wide ones, never moving UR; swap UR and UL with the T perm, then undo the setup. UB and UF take a J perm.

picture.done: R U R' D R U' R' D' U' L' U R U' L U R' F' D2 F U F' D2 F U' R' D' R U R' D R U'

steps.title: Parity
steps.text: An odd number of edge letters leaves two corners swapped by the T perms: after the edges, do this algorithm once, then the corners as usual.

algs.name: Parity
algs.alg: R U' R' U' R U R D R' U' R D' R' U2 R' U'
algs.note: Swaps UB and UL and the corners UBR and UFR: the corners' last letter swaps the edges back.

picture.from: R U R' D R U' R' D' U' L' U R U' L U R' F' D2 F U F' D2 F U' R' D' R U R' D R U' U R U2 R D R' U R D' R' U' R' U R U R'
picture.done: R U R' D R U' R' D' U' L' U R U' L U R' F' D2 F U F' D2 F U' R' D' R U R' D R U'

steps.title: Corners
steps.text: For each corner letter, bring the target to RDF with R, D and F turns that keep UBL, UL and UB, swap UBL and RDF with the modified Y perm, then undo the setup.

333.name: M2 and Old Pochmann
333.summary: Edges by M2, shorter and faster than the T perm: the target set up to UB and swapped with the DF buffer by M2. Corners stay Old Pochmann.

steps.title: Memo
steps.text: Every sticker has a letter (Speffz: A to X, face by face). From the buffer, DF for the edges and UBL for the corners, note the letter where its piece belongs, then where the piece there belongs, until the buffer's piece comes back. Group the letters in pairs and turn each pair into a word or an image.
tips: Edges first, then corners: the memo is read in the order the cube is solved.
When the buffer's piece comes home with pieces still wrong, start a new cycle on one of them and end on it again.
Every second edge letter, read C as W and W as C, I as S and S as I: the M slice is upside down then.

picture.from: R U R' D R U' R' D' U' L' U R U' L U R' F' D2 F U F' D2 F U' R' D' R U R' D R U' M2 U M U2 M' U M2 R2 U R U R' U' R' U' R' U R' D M' U2 M U2 D' F2 M' U M' U M' U2 M U M U M U2 F2 L' E L U L' E' L U'
picture.done: R U R' D R U' R' D' U' L' U R U' L U R' F' D2 F U F' D2 F U' R' D' R U R' D R U' M2 U M U2 M' U M2 R2 U R U R' U' R' U' R' U R' D M' U2 M U2 D' F2 M' U M' U M' U2 M U M U M U2 F2 L' E L U L' E' L U'

steps.title: Edges
steps.text: For each edge letter, bring the target to UB without moving the M slice, do M2, then undo the setup. The M slice's own edges, UF, FU, DB and BD, have algorithms of their own.

picture.done: R U R' D R U' R' D' U' L' U R U' L U R' F' D2 F U F' D2 F U' R' D' R U R' D R U'

steps.title: Parity
steps.text: An odd number of edge letters leaves the M slice half turned: after the edges, do this algorithm once, then the corners as usual.

algs.name: Parity
algs.alg: D' L2 D M2 D' L2 D

picture.from: R U R' D R U' R' D' U' L' U R U' L U R' F' D2 F U F' D2 F U' R' D' R U R' D R U' D' L2 D M2 D' L2 D

steps.title: Corners
steps.text: For each corner letter, bring the target to RDF with R, D and F turns that keep UBL, UL and UB, swap UBL and RDF with the modified Y perm, then undo the setup.

333.name: 3-style
333.summary: The method of the fastest blindfolders: two targets at a time, each pair one commutator from the UF and UFR buffers. Hundreds of cases, learnt a letter at a time.

steps.title: Memo
steps.text: Every sticker has a letter (Speffz: A to X, face by face). From the buffer, UF for the edges and UFR for the corners, note the letter where its piece belongs, then where the piece there belongs, until the buffer's piece comes back. Group the letters in pairs and turn each pair into a word or an image.
tips: Edges first, then corners: the memo is read in the order the cube is solved.
When the buffer's piece comes home with pieces still wrong, start a new cycle on one of them and end on it again.
Each pair of letters is one commutator: learn them a first letter at a time, and drill them in Training → BLD.

picture.from: R U R' D R U' R' D' U' L' U R U' L U R' F' D2 F U F' D2 F U' R' D' R U R' D R U' M2 U M U2 M' U M2 R2 U R U R' U' R' U' R' U R' D M' U2 M U2 D' F2 M' U M' U M' U2 M U M U M U2 F2 L' E L U L' E' L U'
picture.done: R U R' D R U' R' D' U' L' U R U' L U R' F' D2 F U F' D2 F U' R' D' R U R' D R U' M2 U M U2 M' U M2 R2 U R U R' U' R' U' R' U R' D M' U2 M U2 D' F2 M' U M' U M' U2 M U M U M U2 F2 L' E L U L' E' L U'

steps.title: Edges
steps.text: Each pair of edge letters is a commutator that cycles UF with the two targets. An odd last letter is paired with UR.

picture.done: R U R' D R U' R' D' U' L' U R U' L U R' F' D2 F U F' D2 F U' R' D' R U R' D R U'

steps.title: Corners
steps.text: Each pair of corner letters is a commutator that cycles UFR with the two targets.

steps.title: Parity
steps.text: With an odd number of letters, the last corner is left alone: one algorithm swaps UFR with it and UF with UR, which the edges' last pair left swapped.

444.name: r2 and Old Pochmann
444.summary: The 4×4 blindfolded one piece type at a time: the centres by three-cycles, the wings by r2, the corners by Old Pochmann.

steps.title: Memo
steps.text: Trace each piece type from its buffer, in the order you solve them: x-centres, wings, corners. Centres of a colour are alike: a centre may go to any place of its face still wrong.
tips: Set your buffers and your letters in Training → BLD, then train the memo of a scramble there.
Centres take few letters: the places already right are skipped.

steps.title: Centres
steps.text: Cycle three centres at a time with a commutator: moves that bring a target into the top without touching the buffer's place, a turn of the top, then the first moves undone and the turn undone.
tips: Keep the buffer's place on the top face, and set each target up to the slice with the faces that do not touch it.
Write your own commutators down and drill them as you would letter pairs.

steps.title: Wings
steps.text: Swap each wing with the DFr buffer by r2 (the inner slice alone), the target set up to UBr as in M2.

steps.title: Corners
steps.text: The corners are the 3×3's: Old Pochmann from UBL, with the outer layers only.
tips: Learn Old Pochmann's corners on the 3×3 first: the setups are the same.

555.name: r2 and Old Pochmann
555.summary: The 5×5 blindfolded one piece type at a time: the +-centres and x-centres by three-cycles, the wings by r2, the midges by M2 and the corners by Old Pochmann.

steps.title: Memo
steps.text: Trace each piece type from its buffer, in the order you solve them: +-centres, x-centres, wings, midges, corners. Centres of a colour are alike: a centre may go to any place of its face still wrong.
tips: Set your buffers and your letters in Training → BLD, then train the memo of a scramble there.
Centres take few letters: the places already right are skipped.

steps.title: Centres
steps.text: Cycle three centres at a time with a commutator: moves that bring a target into the top without touching the buffer's place, a turn of the top, then the first moves undone and the turn undone.
tips: Keep the buffer's place on the top face, and set each target up to the slice with the faces that do not touch it.
Write your own commutators down and drill them as you would letter pairs.

steps.title: Wings
steps.text: Swap each wing with the DFr buffer by r2 (the inner slice alone), the target set up to UBr as in M2.

steps.title: Midges
steps.text: The 5×5's middle edges are the 3×3's edges: solve them with M2 from DF, the middle slice alone.
tips: Learn M2 on the 3×3 first: the targets and their setups are the same.

steps.title: Corners
steps.text: The corners are the 3×3's: Old Pochmann from UBL, with the outer layers only.
tips: Learn Old Pochmann's corners on the 3×3 first: the setups are the same.
